questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Seemed like a movie destination, Boston is known for having a lot of colleges and students, fun campus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was pretty smooth. Got a lot right before leaving, so i knew where to go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Went to an introduction meeting where they told us a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You just got it assigned randomly. I got a dorm apartment with one other roommate and it was great.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could buy a meal plan, but i had a kitchen in my dorm, so i cooked and then bought some individual meals at school when i wanted to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The experience really differ from dorm to dorm, but to be open minded with a roommate.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Could pick some courses before but for a few of them i had to have prerequisites, so i had to wait to talk to an advisor when i landed. Super chill. A few of the courses i wanted was initially filled up, but then i emailed the professors and they pretty much all gave me a spot so i had plenty of options.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Advisors at the introduction meeting and people i could go to or email after if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got them all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress to much before you go there, try out different classes and find some that you like, take more than you need, then you can drop one when you get to know them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: So much more homework, and there is participation grades so you have to talk more. But that created great classroom discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Memory and Media, What's Popular About Popular Movies?, Independent American Film and The Cultural Politics of Film and TV History

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Cultural Politics of Film and TV History was by far the best. Loved the films, loved the class, loved the professor he was really great, really nice and really knowledgable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Lots of expenses before you leave, like vaccines, language tests, documents and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Living in Boston is really expensive, so going out to eat and buying groceries it not cheap. Going to different sports events was way cheaper than i expected so that was great!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts, lots of clubs and sports options. Join a club just for the fun of it. They host parties and formals and get togethers.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to all the sport games, it is so worth it. And go the parties and formals. Go to line dancing at Landsdown. Travel if you can, take the bus to New York. And all the museums are free for students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Miami on spring break was a lot of fun. Puerto Rico was beautiful. Austin Texas was amazing highly recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open, talk to lots of people. Meet friends of friends, go for coffee.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Did not have any issues.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything was just like i have seen in the movies it was wonderful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Spend time with the other exchange students, it is much more fun to experience everything for the first time together. 
Honestly i spend more money than i thought i would, so be preparred.
For me it was pass/fail, and the teachers were really nice, so do not be too stressed out about the school work. Talk to the teachers about what you need to do, do your best but have fun too.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to all the events you can at school just because.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends, travelling and so so many new experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did get a bit homesick in the middle, so call your mom and it will get better.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
